title: WORKSHEET 3
subject: Present Simple and Present Continuous
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 3: Present Simple and Present Continuous

sections.instruction: Read the paragraphs and answer the questions:
sections.contextText:
1) Hello! My name is Douglas Hunter. I'm a pilot for British Airlines. I fly planes. I am not working today. I am playing golf. It is my favorite sport.

2) He is Gordon Lester. He is a champion jockey. He rides racehorses, but he isn't riding a racehorse now. He is dancing with his wife.

3) They are Bob and Michael. They teach English in a school. They aren't teaching now. They are in the pub. They're talking and laughing.

4) She is Rosalind Graham. She is a ballet dancer. She dances for Royal Ballet. She isn't dancing now. She is having a bath.

questions.prompt: Douglas: What is his name?
Douglas: What does he do?
acceptedAnswers: He is a pilot for British Airlines.
He is a pilot. He flies planes.
questions.explanation: What does he do? = his job (present simple)

questions.prompt: Douglas: What is he doing now?
Douglas: What is his favorite sport?
Gordon: What is his name?
Gordon: What does he do?
acceptedAnswers: He is a champion jockey. He rides racehorses.
questions.explanation: What does he do? = his job (present simple)

questions.prompt: Gordon: Is he a good jockey?
acceptedAnswers: Yes, he is. He is a champion jockey.
Yes, he is a champion jockey.
Yes, he is a good jockey.
questions.explanation: He is a champion jockey → yes

questions.prompt: Gordon: Where is he now?
questions.modelAnswer: He is at a dance with his wife.
questions.explanation: The text only says he is dancing with his wife.

questions.prompt: Gordon: What is he doing?
acceptedAnswers: He is dancing with his wife.

questions.prompt: Gordon: Who is he with?
questions.explanation: He is dancing with his wife.

questions.prompt: Bob and Michael: Who are they?
acceptedAnswers: They are Bob and Michael. They are teachers.

questions.prompt: Bob and Michael: Do they teach?
acceptedAnswers: Yes, they do. They teach English.

questions.prompt: Bob and Michael: What do they teach?
acceptedAnswers: They teach English in a school.

questions.prompt: Bob and Michael: Where are they now?
Bob and Michael: What are they doing now?
acceptedAnswers: They are talking and laughing in the pub.

questions.prompt: Rosalind: What is her name?
Rosalind: What does she do?
acceptedAnswers: She dances for the Royal Ballet.
She is a ballet dancer. She dances for Royal Ballet.
questions.explanation: What does she do? = her job

questions.prompt: Rosalind: Is she dancing now?
acceptedAnswers: No, she isn't. She is having a bath.

questions.prompt: Rosalind: What is she doing?
acceptedAnswers: She is having a bath now.

sections.instruction: Write DON’T, DOESN’T, ISN’T, AREN’T or AM NOT in the blank space in each sentence: (Examples: a. He isn’t listening to the radio right now. b. He doesn’t listen to the radio every evening.)

questions.prompt: c. We [gap] watching a television program now.
d. We [gap] watch television every day.
e. They [gap] study their lessons after class.
f. They [gap] studying their lessons right now.
g. It [gap] raining very hard right at the moment.
h. It [gap] rain very much during the summer.
i. Mr. Johnson [gap] eating his lunch now.
j. Mr. Johnson [gap] always eat at that place.
k. I [gap] see any students in that room.
questions.explanation: I + don't + base verb (see is stative)

questions.prompt: l. I [gap] hear anyone in the hall now.
questions.explanation: hear is stative; base verb → don't

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences with your own ideas (present simple or present continuous):

questions.prompt: Every Monday my father [gap] because [gap].
questions.modelAnswer: Every Monday my father gets up early because he starts work at 7 o'clock.

questions.prompt: Linda usually [gap] but she [gap] today.
questions.modelAnswer: Linda usually walks to school but she is going by bus today.

questions.prompt: I want to buy a [gap] because [gap].
questions.modelAnswer: I want to buy a new bike because my old bike is broken.

questions.prompt: My teacher often [gap] but today [gap].
questions.modelAnswer: My teacher often gives us homework but today she isn't giving us any.

questions.prompt: At the moment the children [gap]. They often [gap].
questions.modelAnswer: At the moment the children are playing in the garden. They often play there after school.
questions.explanation: at the moment → continuous; often → simple

sections.instruction: Read the following text and answer the questions. Questions 11–15: write True or False.
sections.contextText:
My name is Kate O'Hara. I live on a farm with my mother and father. I like it but I work very hard. Every morning I wake up at five o'clock and feed the horses. Then I can go back to the house. Mum makes breakfast at 5:30 and I'm not late for breakfast because I don't like cold eggs. After breakfast I help dad for an hour. Then I have a shower and get ready for school. The school bus leaves at 8:15. I leave home at 8:00.
After school I can watch TV for an hour. Then we have our dinner. We have chicken for dinner but I hate it. I eat it because mum gets angry. After dinner I do my homework. Then I go out and feed the horses. I go to bed early because I'm always very tired at the end of the day.

questions.prompt: Where does Kate live?
acceptedAnswers: She lives on a farm with her mother and father.
She lives on a farm with her parents.

questions.prompt: What time does she get up every morning?
acceptedAnswers: She gets up at five o'clock.
She wakes up at five o'clock.
questions.explanation: Every morning I wake up at five o'clock.

questions.prompt: Who makes breakfast every morning?
Why isn't she late for breakfast?
acceptedAnswers: Because she doesn't like cold eggs.
She isn't late because she doesn't like cold eggs.

questions.prompt: When does she have a shower?
acceptedAnswers: She has a shower after she helps her dad.
After she helps her dad for an hour.
She has a shower after helping her dad.
She has a shower after she helps her dad for an hour.
questions.explanation: After breakfast she helps dad, then has a shower.

questions.prompt: What time does she catch the school bus?
acceptedAnswers: She catches the school bus at 8:15.
She catches the school bus at a quarter past eight.

questions.prompt: How long can she watch TV?
acceptedAnswers: She can watch TV for an hour.
She can watch TV for one hour.

questions.prompt: What do they have for dinner?
When does she do her homework?
acceptedAnswers: She does her homework after dinner.
questions.explanation: After dinner I do my homework.

questions.prompt: Why does she go to bed early?
acceptedAnswers: Because she is always very tired at the end of the day.
Because she is always very tired.

questions.prompt: She doesn't like the farm. (True or False?)
questions.explanation: “I like it but I work very hard.”

questions.prompt: Kate doesn't work very hard. (True or False?)
Kate has a shower before 8:15. (True or False?)
questions.explanation: She showers, then leaves home at 8:00.

questions.prompt: Kate's mother doesn't like chicken. (True or False?)
questions.explanation: It is Kate who hates chicken.

questions.prompt: After dinner Kate feeds the horses. (True or False?)
questions.explanation: After dinner: homework, then she feeds the horses.

sections.instruction: Change the following sentences into POSITIVE (+), NEGATIVE (-) and QUESTION (?) form:

questions.prompt: You know the answer. → (-)
You know the answer. → (?)
He has breakfast at 8 o'clock. → (-)
acceptedAnswers: He doesn't have breakfast at 8 o'clock.
He doesn't have breakfast at eight o'clock.

questions.prompt: He has breakfast at 8 o'clock. → (?)
acceptedAnswers: Does he have breakfast at 8 o'clock?
Does he have breakfast at eight o'clock?

questions.prompt: Some schoolgirls don't wear uniforms. → (+)
Some schoolgirls don't wear uniforms. → (?)
Does she cut her husband's hair? → (+)
Does she cut her husband's hair? → (-)
acceptedAnswers: She doesn't cut her husband's hair.

questions.prompt: She does her homework every day. → (-)
acceptedAnswers: She doesn't do her homework every day.
She doesn't do her homework everyday.

questions.prompt: She does her homework every day. → (?)
acceptedAnswers: Does she do her homework every day?
Does she do her homework everyday?

sections.instruction: Supply PRESENT CONTINUOUS TENSE in the blanks:

questions.prompt: He [gap] (teach) his son to ride a bike.
A: Why [gap] Ann [gap] (wear) her new dress? B: Because she [gap] (have) a party tonight.
Cindy usually does the shopping, but I [gap] (do) it today because she is ill.
She [gap] (not / work), she [gap] (swim) in the river.
A: [gap] Tom [gap] (clean) his shoes now? B: No, he [gap]. He [gap] (tidy) his room. A: Where is his brother? B: He is in the garden, he [gap] (water) the flowers.
acceptedAnswers: Is / cleaning / isn't / is tidying|'s tidying / is watering|'s watering
questions.explanation: Is … -ing? No, he isn't. He is + -ing
